mono-7006.d: The stars above Baikonur at the moment Sputnik 1 lifted off: every star to magnitude 4.8 in its real place, the constellation figures, the horizon as the circle. Every mark stands for something real.

mono-7008.d: The moon's phase for every day of 1969, the year of the first landing, month by month, computed for midnight UTC. A reference sheet you can wear.

mono-7015.d: Where the sun stands at noon by the clock, every day of a year at Greenwich: the figure of eight the tilt of the earth and its elliptical orbit trace, computed from the solar equations. A reference sheet you can wear.

mono-7016.d: How long the sun is up in Tromsø on each day of the year, from sunrise to sunset, one line every third day, computed from the sun's declination at 69.6° north. Exact to the last figure shown.

mono-7020.d: The orbit of Halley's comet to scale, with its position at sixteen equal steps of its 76-year period: the lines from the sun sweep equal areas, Kepler's second law, bunched where the comet races past the sun. Computed, not invented.

mono-7024.d: The lancet arch set out as a mason draws it: two arcs, radius longer than the span, centres outside it, the voussoir joints radiating from the compass centres, marked with the construction lines. Plotted from the numbers.

mono-7026.d: The horseshoe arch set out as a mason draws it: one arc carried past the half circle, centre above the springing, the voussoir joints radiating from the compass centres, marked with the construction lines. Every mark stands for something real.

mono-7053.d: The ISO 216 A series: A0 of one square metre, each size half the one before at the same proportion, one to the square root of two. Measured before it was drawn.

mono-7078.d: The bridge rectifier as a schematic in standard symbols. Four diodes in a ring feeding a load: whichever way the supply swings, current flows through the load the same way. Measured before it was drawn.

mono-7085.d: An aneroid barometer's face from 28 to 31 inches of mercury, with the traditional words from Stormy to Very Dry. Drawn as line work. Computed, not invented.

mono-7086.d: A VU meter's scale from −20 to +3 volume units, marked where a needle driven by the voltage points (0 VU at 71% of the swing), with the red zone ticked past zero. Drawn as line work. Computed, not invented.

mono-7091.d: The Smith chart radio engineers use to match impedances: circles of constant resistance and arcs of constant reactance, drawn from their equations inside the unit circle. A reference sheet you can wear.

mono-7100.d: The alphabet in a five-by-seven dot matrix, the grid of character LCDs and dot-matrix printers, lit dots full and the rest pinpricks. Measured before it was drawn.
